title: Strict roots target with the adjunct formula for any residue lift
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and invertible on an arbitrary scheme $W$, and let $D$ be a simultaneous derived reduction of scalar extension [def-sfb-diagonal-system-interface], using [lem-sfb-canonical-sheaf-ext]. Write $U$ for forgetting p-adic scalars, $F_n$ for restriction from $\mathbf Z/\ell^{n+1}$ to $\mathbf Z_\ell$, and $G_m^{comp}$ for the comparison pullback of the etale units sheaf. There exist a strict constant-p-adic system $H$, an isomorphism $roots:H\circ U\simeq(\mu_{\ell^{n+1}})_n$ to the actual roots tower [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], an isomorphism $b:D.T(G_m^{comp}[1])\simeq H[2]$, and level isomorphisms $t_n:H_n\simeq F_n((\mathbf Z/\ell^{n+1})(1))$, with $U(t_n)=roots_n$ followed by the canonical roots-to-line map [def-sfb-cartier-reduction-data]. For any level $n$, abelian source $S$, canonical invertible source counit $a$, residue sheaf $Q$, isomorphism $s:D.ordinary(S)_n\simeq F_nQ$ and map $g:S\to forget(Q)$ equal to the quotient-adjunction unit under $s$, take any $f\in Ext^1(S,G_m^{comp})$. If a residue class $e\in Ext^2(Q,(\mathbf Z/\ell^{n+1})(1))$ has restriction equal to evaluation of $a^{-1}D.T(f)b$ under $s,t_n$, then its scalar adjunct is $-f\kappa_n$, where $\kappa_n$ is the positive Kummer class preceded by the units comparison. This is a conditional compatibility equation for any supplied residue lift; existence of such a lift is not a conclusion.

source.place: Step (3), target paragraph, and step (4), derived-adjunction naturality. This separates the Kummer computation of the adjunct from the independent existence of a residue-linear lift.

proof.text: Use canonical sheaf abelian structures and the already fixed small Ext witnesses throughout.

Compute simultaneous reduction of comparison units on a common K-flat resolution. The constant prime-power two-term resolution, Kummer exactness and exact site comparison identify its only cohomology with the actual roots kernel in degree minus one.

Multiplication by the prime in degree minus one and identity in degree zero give the coefficient-resolution transitions. The induced kernel transition is the prime-power roots map. Good truncation in the strict system category gives H, roots and b; choose the negative normalized Kummer comparison. The canonical roots-to-line maps give t and the full underlying-map equation.

Compare evaluation with residue scalar extension on the same resolution, then forget scalars. The source counit and ordinary quotient adjunction identify the unit with g; the target normalization gives minus the compared positive Kummer unit. Naturality for f computes the scalar adjunct of its evaluated arrow. For any supplied e whose restriction is that arrow, exact-functor composition identifies its adjunct with this computation. No claim of fullness on derived morphisms is made.
